newsitem.title: USA: Illinois, Missouri study Union/CIPSCO merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Illinois, Missouri study Union/CIPSCO merger plan.

text.p: llinois and Missouri regulators are reviewing a proposed merger between Union Electric Co and CIPSCO Inc to determine whether it might stiffle open competition in the states' electricity markets.
A spokesman for Missouri Public Service Commission said it has scheduled a hearing Feb 11 to gather public views on the issue of "market power."
The five Missouri commissioners voted unanimously to examine the issue after recent recommendations from their own staff and the state's Office of Public Counsel.
Illinois Commerce Commission also last week voted to begin examining the issue of the market power with the Union/CIPSCO merger.

Nationally, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) developed a screen test to help determine whether any specific mergers might hamper competition as the U.S. moves toward a deregulated electricity industry.
Last month, CIPSCO and Union Electric asked FERC for an exemption from the screening process.
"The FERC staff recommended we be exempted," said Union Electric spokeswoman Susan Gallagher, adding the exhaustive procedures could delay the completion of merger.
A decision on whether exemption will be granted now rests with FERC's commissioners and is expected some time this month.

The merger of the two Midwest utilities, announced Aug 14, 1995, would create a new holding company called Ameren Corp, with annual revenues of nearly $3 billion and over 1.5 million electric customers across Missouri and in central and south-central Illinois.
